The TVB-O ontology is the formal, machine-readable backbone of the TVB-O data model. It provides the shared vocabulary and axioms used by the Python package, the Odoo platform, and every external interoperability target (NeuroML, openMINDS, BIDS).

## Browse the specification

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
The [W3C-style specification](https://virtual-twin.github.io/tvbo/ontology/spec/index-en.html), with a [WebVOWL visualisation](https://virtual-twin.github.io/tvbo/ontology/spec/webvowl/index.html#ontology), is generated by Widoco from the released ontology every time the documentation is published.
:::

## Stable identifiers

`https://w3id.org/tvbo/` is the namespace of every TVB-O term, and every IRI in it dereferences:

| IRI | Resolves to |
|-----|-------------|
| `https://w3id.org/tvbo/` | This page in a browser; the whole ontology to an RDF client, as Turtle, JSON-LD, RDF/XML or N-Triples by its `Accept` header |
| `https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl` | The ontology IRI: the current release's merged OWL file |
| `https://w3id.org/tvbo/0.9.0/tvbo.owl` | A version IRI: the file attached to that release, as are `tvb-o-struct.owl` and `tvb-o.shacl.ttl` |
| `https://w3id.org/tvbo/Dynamics` | A schema term: a class, slot or enumeration |
| `https://w3id.org/tvbo/models/JansenRit` | A curated record, at `/<collection>/<file stem>` |

A term IRI leads to the term's page on the [TVB-O platform](https://tvbo.charite.de/ontology/models/JansenRit), which returns the term's description as HTML to a browser and as Turtle, JSON-LD, RDF/XML or N-Triples by `Accept` header, or by a `.ttl`, `.jsonld`, `.rdf` or `.nt` suffix on the path. Link to the w3id IRI, never to the address it redirects to: the IRI is what stays fixed.

A collection is the database folder a record is filed in: `models`, `coupling_functions`, `networks`, `atlases`, `experiments`, `studies`, `observation_models`, `functions`, `integrators`, `graph_generators`, `continuations`, `coordinate_spaces`, `software` and `themes`. A record is named by its file stem, which is unique in its collection however deep the file sits; an atlas's is its BIDS stem (`atlases/tpl-MNI152NLin2009c_atlas-DesikanKilliany_desc-ranked_dseg`). Schema terms never sit under a collection, so a record and a term cannot claim the same IRI. A spec names a record the same way, as `iri: tvbo:models/JansenRit`, in every collection but `coordinate_spaces`, whose records only the ontology carries. `tvbo migrate-iris` rewrites specs that name a record by its `name:`, by an older singular scope (`tvbo:observation/…`) or unscoped.

## Downloads

| Artefact | Format | What it is |
|----------|--------|------------|
| [`tvbo.owl`](https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl) | OWL/XML | Merged T-box, axioms and A-box, ELK-materialised |
| [`tvb-o-axioms.ttl`](https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvb-o-axioms.ttl) | Turtle | Hand-authored axiom layer (technical, biological, dynamical) |
| [`tvb-o.shacl.ttl`](https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvb-o.shacl.ttl) | Turtle (SHACL) | Validation shapes generated from the LinkML schema |

Each [GitHub release](https://github.com/virtual-twin/tvbo/releases) carries its `tvbo.owl`, the structural T-box `tvb-o-struct.owl`, `tvb-o.shacl.ttl` and their checksums, and the [`tvbo` Python package](../../installation.html) ships `tvbo.owl` under `tvbo/data/ontology/`.

## How the specification is built

The pipeline is fully reproducible from the LinkML schema:

```bash
make gen-owl       # tvb-o-struct.owl  (T-box from LinkML)
make gen-shacl     # tvb-o.shacl.ttl   (validation shapes)
make gen-abox      # tvb-o-data.ttl    (A-box from YAML database)
make gen-merged    # tvbo.owl          (ROBOT merge + ELK reasoner)
make gen-widoco    # docs/_site/ontology/spec/ (Widoco HTML + WebVOWL, after quarto render)
```

The hand-authored axiom layer (`ontology/tvb-o-axioms.ttl`) extends the generated T-box with categories that cannot be expressed in LinkML alone:

1. **Technical axioms**: backends, capabilities, tasks and requirements.
2. **Biological axioms**: anatomical, cellular and neurotransmitter substrate grounding via UBERON/CL/GO/CHEBI/MESH cross-references.
3. **Dynamical axioms**: qualitative regimes, bifurcations, attractors, stochasticity character and model features.
4. **Per-model briefs**: for each canonical mean-field model, a concise set of axioms summarising its biological substrate, phase-space dimensionality, and dynamical repertoire.

See the [methods chapter](../../2-specify/SpecificationReference.qmd) for the full ontological-engineering rationale. The active restructuring roadmap is tracked internally.

## Citing TVB-O

Please cite the ontology by its persistent identifier and the preprint that describes it:

> **TVB-O, The Virtual Brain Ontology.** `https://w3id.org/tvbo/`, <https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.19.689211>
